newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Advanced Micro calls busy again.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Advanced Micro calls busy again.

text.p: Options on shares of Advanced Micro Devices Inc drew attention for a second consecutive day Tuesday as the stock extended its gains to break through the 30 strike price, traders said.
By about 1330 CST/1930 GMT, the chip maker's stock was ahead four at 33 on consolidated volume of more than 7.4 million shares. Advanced Micro rose nearly two points Monday.
Late Monday, the company reported a fourth quarter net loss of $0.15 a share, smaller than the $0.19 a share loss analysts had expected. It earned $0.07 a share in the year ago fourth quarter.
Soundview Financial Group initiated coverage of the company on Tuesday with short-term buy and long-term hold ratings.
Among the Advanced Micro options, which trade on the Pacific Stock Exchange, the January 30 and February 30 saw the most activity, with 6,530 and 5,375 contracts changing hands, respectively.
Other busy calls included the February 35s, April 30s and July 35s.
The most active put was the January 30, which traded about 430 contracts.
Traders said investors appeared to be taking some profits in the January calls and establishing positions in the Februarys, Aprils and Julys.

"It's just people closing that were betting on an up move closing out longs," one trader at the PSE said, referring to the January call activity. "The stock's had a really good move and they probably have been long for a long time."
Last Friday the stock bounced off 26-3/4.
"There haven't been any rolls," the trader added. "It's pretty much customers closing out and buying the Feb 35s, the July 35s and the April 35s."
Options on another chip maker's stock, Intel Corp, also remained busy as that stock continued its recent strong run.
Intel shares rose 2-1/4 points to 149-1/8 on more than 10 million shares. The stock reached 149-3/8 intraday, a new record high.
Intel is scheduled to report quarterly earnings after the market closes.
The Intel January 150 call was most active in the group, with volume of about 10,270 contracts. Open interest through Monday, which included an add of 1,525, was 15,400 contracts.
The Intel January 140 call, 145 call and 155 call each traded more than 5,000 contracts.
With the January series set to expire at the end of the week, several of the February and April calls saw solid action, with volume on the February 150 call nearing 3,000 contracts.

Among Intel puts, the January 135 was most active, with volume of 4,400. The option, which still had 6,572 contracts open through Monday and increasing odds of expiring worthless, was down 1/4 at 3/8. ((--G.Crawford, 3124088750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
